title: [console 17.0.0-rc.0 @4a4829d0] Edit modal: a visibleWhen that flips false→true when the record lands wipes every rendered select's value, and the form latches broken
body:
## Summary

In the record **edit** modal, if a field's `visibleWhen` flips **false → true** at the moment the record's `defaultValues` land, every **currently-rendered `select`** loses its value: RHF's `_defaultValues` still holds the correct value, but `_formValues` is `''`. Because one of the wiped selects is usually the very field the predicate reads, the predicate flips back to false, the conditional fields hide again, and the form **latches in the broken state** — it never self-heals.

Net effect for the user: opening a record and pressing Update without touching anything fails validation ("field is required"), or silently submits an empty enum to the server.

Same family as #2959 (form state destroyed by a remount), but a different trigger — no tabs involved, and the record here is not multi-section-dependent.

## Repro

Object with (a) a `select` field, and (b) any field whose `visibleWhen` references it:

```ts
category: {
  type: 'select',
  options: [ {label:'00 Production', value:'production'}, {label:'01 Quality', value:'quality'}, /* … */ ],
  defaultValue: 'production',
},
status: { type: 'select', options: [ /* … */ ], defaultValue: 'pending' },

need_quality: {
  type: 'boolean',
  visibleWhen: P`record.category == "production" || record.need_quality == true`,
},
```

1. Open a record whose stored `category` **is** `"production"` (so the predicate is TRUE once data lands).
2. Detail page → **Edit**.
3. Look at `category` and `status`.

**Expected**: `category = "00 Production"`, `status` = the record's status, and `need_quality` visible.
**Actual**: both selects render the placeholder (empty), and `need_quality` stays hidden.

A record whose `category` is anything else (predicate stays FALSE throughout) renders correctly.

## Observed runtime state

Read off the live React tree (walk the fiber from the select up to the node carrying `control` + `getValues`), 3/3 identical runs:

```
_defaultValues.category = "production"     ← the form DID receive the right defaults
_formValues.category    = ""               ← runtime value was wiped
lostKeys                = "category,status"
```

`lostKeys` = keys that are non-empty in `_defaultValues` but empty/absent in `_formValues`. It is **exactly the rendered selects**. In the same form, text / number / datetime / lookup values all survive. A third select in the schema (`inspection_status`) is *not* in the list — it happened to be hidden at that moment.

Server data is not implicated: the modal's own `findOne` returns 48 keys with `category:"production"`, `status:"pending"`.

## This is a race — and here is the proof

Same page, **no reload**, open the edit modal three times in a row:

```
open #1: category=""            status=""                                    selects=2
open #2: category="production"  status="pending"  inspection_status="pending"  selects=3
open #3: category="production"  status="pending"  inspection_status="pending"  selects=3
```

From open #2 the modal already has the record cached, so `defaultValues` are present on the **first** render — no flip, no wipe, and the conditional field renders as it should (select count 2 → 3).

So the trigger is: modal mounts → `findOne` still in flight → `defaultValues = {}` → `ruleRecord` seeds every field to `null` → predicate FALSE → conditional fields render hidden → data lands → `form.reset(defaultValues)` → predicate TRUE → the rendered field set changes → the already-mounted selects get clobbered to `''` → predicate FALSE again → latched.

## Falsifiable experiment (it follows the predicate, not the value)

Flip the predicate from `record.category == "production"` to `record.category == "quality"` and change nothing else:

```
production record: category="production"  status="pending"   ← now correct
quality    record: category=""            status=""          ← now broken
```

3/3 stable. Removing the `visibleWhen` clauses altogether also fixes it, and the conditional fields then render normally.

## Scope observed

| Situation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| predicate flips **hidden → visible** when the record lands | **wiped** |
| predicate flips **visible → hidden** | fine |
| predicate constant (either way) | fine |
| field types affected | **`select` only** — text / number / datetime / lookup keep their values |
| section grouping | irrelevant — reproduced with the conditional field in a group that also holds unconditional fields, so no section divider appears/disappears |

Across four objects in the same app only the heaviest one reproduces deterministically (48 fields, ~12 `populate` joins on the detail fetch) — consistent with the race framing: the slower the record load relative to first paint, the more reliably it latches. On lighter objects the same predicate shape is fine, and even the heavy one occasionally converges correctly.

## Ruled out

The per-option cascade clear is **not** the path here. These fields have no per-option `visibleWhen` and no `dependsOn`, so:

- `resolveCascadingOptions` (`packages/core/src/evaluator/optionRules.ts`) returns the full set, `gated:false`;
- `isValueStillOffered` is therefore true;
- `SelectField`'s clear effect (`packages/fields/src/widgets/SelectField.tsx`, the `[options, gated]` effect) and the form renderer's equivalent both bail out at the `hasOptionPredicate || dependsOn` guard.

Both of those also write `undefined`, whereas the value we observe is the **string `''`** — which points at a different writer.

## Hypothesis (not verified — flagging, not asserting)

`''` is what a native `<select>` reports when no option matches. The shadcn/Radix `Select` renders a hidden native `<select name=…>` mirror for form integration. If the field-set change causes RHF to (re-)attach the field ref to that mirror element while Radix's own value is momentarily unset, `getValues()` would read `''` back out of the DOM and write it into `_formValues`. That would explain both why only `select` is affected and why the written value is `''` rather than the `undefined` every explicit clear path uses. Worth checking before designing the fix.

## Suggested direction

Any one of these closes it:

- don't render the form until `defaultValues` for an edit-mode record have resolved (the modal already knows it is loading);
- evaluate the field rules against `defaultValues` merged over the watched values, rather than an all-`null` seed, so the predicate does not start FALSE for a record that will satisfy it;
- after a `reset`, reconcile `_formValues` against `_defaultValues` for fields that were remounted by a visibility change.

## Downstream damage worth noting

1. The wipe is recorded as a user edit — the modal's dirty guard fires, so **Cancel prompts "discard changes?"** on a form the user never touched.
2. If the user just presses Update, the server rejects with a message about the *other* field (in our app: `派工单状态流转非法：pending → 。` i.e. "illegal status transition: pending → ."), which points at the state machine and completely masks the real cause. This cost us a full debugging session before we found the form was submitting empty enums.

## Environment

- `@objectstack/console` **17.0.0-rc.0**, `dist/.objectui-sha` = **4a4829d0ef3926e9b55757bfb1e369d6dca61ac2**
- `@objectstack/*` 17.0.0-rc.0, single-tenant, SqlDriver (better-sqlite3)
- Chromium (Playwright), admin session, desktop viewport
